Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice E.S.Indiresh
 Oral Judgment
Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

2. This appeal is preferred by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation, assailing the judgment and award dated 13.07.2022 in MVC No.226/2019, on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-II at Yadgiri NC: 2026:KHC-K:1005 HC-KAR (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal'),
awarding compensation to the claimant.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Having taken note of the submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties, it is not in dispute that, the claimant has sustained grievous injuries on account of road traffic accident occurred on 30.12.2018.

sentences.text: Taking note of the reasons assigned by the Tribunal and by looking into the evidence of PW.2 - treating doctor, I am of the view that the Tribunal ought to have taken the disability at 15% by looking into the grievous injuries sustained by the claimant, particularly, with regard to fracture of inferior pubic rami.

In that view of the matter, following the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the income of claimant has to be taken at Rs.11,750/- per month and by applying the appropriate multiplier of 17, the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,59,550/- towards loss of future income.

Taking into consideration the other aspects NC:
2026:KHC-K:1005 HC-KAR of the matter, I am of the view that, no interference is called for insofar as other heads are concerned.

5. Accordingly, the claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation as follows:
 Heads Amount Pain and suffering Rs.50,000/-
Loss of earnings during laid up Rs.30,000/-
period Loss of amenities Rs.20,000/-
Loss of future of earnings Rs.3,59,550/-
Towards food and nourishment and Rs.30,000/-
attendant charges

Medical expenses Rs.5,45,088/-
Total Rs.10,34,638/-
Less: awarded by Tribunal Rs.8,38,288/-
Enhancement Rs.1,96,350/-
Thus, the clamant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,96,350/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

6. Insofar as liability to pay the compensation is concerned, on careful consideration of the discussion made by the Tribunal at paragraph No.22, wherein, it is disclosed that, the cheque issued by respondent No.1 for NC: 2026:KHC-K:1005 HC-KAR payment of premium amount has been dishonored due to insufficient funds in the account, however, respondent No.3 - Insurance Company has also issued intimation about dishonour of cheque through post after receipt of cheque returned memo with his banker.

Hence, in view of the settled principle of law by this Court and the Hon'ble Supreme Court, respondent No. - Insurance Company is directed to pay the compensation to the claimant/appellant and thereafter, recover the same from respondent Nos.1 and 2.
7.

In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER I.
The appeal is allowed in part.
II. The appellant/claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,96,350/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
